scenes.text: Without Spring, your code creates a repository, then passes it into a service.
scenes.phonemes: wɪðˌaʊt spɹˈɪŋ, jʊɹ kˈoʊd kɹiːˈeɪts ɐ ɹᵻpˈɑːzɪtˌɔːɹi, ðˈɛn pˈæsᵻz ɪɾ ˌɪntʊ ɐ sˈɜːvɪs.

scenes.text: With Spring, you register bean definitions. The container uses them to create managed objects and wire their dependencies.
scenes.phonemes: wɪð spɹˈɪŋ, juː ɹˈɛdʒɪstɚ bˈiːn dˌɛfɪnˈɪʃənz. ðə kəntˈeɪnɚ jˈuːsᵻz ðˌɛm tə kɹiːˈeɪt mˈænɪdʒd ˈɑːbdʒɛkts ænd wˈaɪɚ ðɛɹ dᵻpˈɛndənsiz.

scenes.text: Here, the service bean asks for a repository. Spring supplies that bean.
scenes.phonemes: hˈɪɹ, ðə sˈɜːvɪs bˈiːn ˈæsks fɚɹɚ ɹᵻpˈɑːzɪtˌɔːɹi. spɹˈɪŋ səplˈaɪz ðæt bˈiːn.

scenes.text: Your application calls get bean to request the ready service. In our Java run, its repository is the same bean from the container.
scenes.phonemes: jʊɹ ˌæplɪkˈeɪʃən kˈɔːlz ɡɛt bˈiːn tə ɹᵻkwˈɛst ðə ɹˈɛdi sˈɜːvɪs. ɪn ˌaʊɚ dʒˈɑːvɚ ɹˈʌn, ɪts ɹᵻpˈɑːzɪtˌɔːɹi ɪz ðə sˈeɪm bˈiːn fɹʌmðə kəntˈeɪnɚ.

scenes.text: Your app starts Spring with Config. Spring calls Config’s bean methods, creates Repo, and wires Service. Your app retrieves the ready service. Managed beans only.
scenes.phonemes: jʊɹ ˈæp stˈɑːɹts spɹˈɪŋ wɪð kənfˈɪɡ. spɹˈɪŋ kˈɔːlz kənfˈɪɡz bˈiːn mˈɛθədz, kɹiːˈeɪts ɹˈiːpoʊ, ænd wˈaɪɚz sˈɜːvɪs. jʊɹ ˈæp ɹᵻtɹˈiːvz ðə ɹˈɛdi sˈɜːvɪs. mˈænɪdʒd bˈiːnz ˈoʊnli.
